answer.rationale: Three concurrent signals — p99 write-path latency at 5× target, a release shipped 2 hours ago, and settlement traffic at daily peak with heavy writes — most closely match the pattern in memory_b1 (day 18): a release caused an error spike and rollback restored stability without customer impact. The timing correlation (release 2h ago, latency climbing for 90 minutes) strongly suggests the release is the causal factor. Rolling back reverts to the prior known-stable build and eliminates the suspected cause, preserving customer writes throughout (per memory_b1, rollback completed without customer impact). This directly serves the objective of maximizing sustained availability without losing writes. Alternative interventions (add_capacity, regional_failover) address capacity or locality, not a bad build; circuit breaker or read-replica routing would not fix the underlying write-path regression. Verification budget is spent on memory_b1 because it is the closest precedent and its archived detail (rollback procedure, customer-impact outcome) will confirm the safe rollback path under load.
